label: Finite interpretations and one general equivalence
meaning: Finite interpretations and one general equivalence. On a Black-style single-mover carrier, where every non-first being has one shared non-pure determination, unrestricted perfection, strict pure actuality, identity of purely determined indiscernibles and at-most-one hold with an actual first mover, while identity of real indiscernibles fails. With determination-free inert rows, the two pure-act premises and at-most-one hold while identity of purely determined indiscernibles fails. If only first movers are purely determined, then under the two pure-act premises identity of purely determined indiscernibles is equivalent to at-most-one first mover. Each of the three premises of the narrower uniqueness theorem is omitted in turn with the other two retained and at-most-one failing. Satisfiability of encoded bundles, not metaphysical possibility.
